Compute the statistical mode of a vector

Source: R/calc_mode.R
calc_mode.Rd

Returns the most frequent value in a vector, optionally handling ties in different ways. Missing values are ignored.

Usage

calc_mode(x, ties = c("first", "all", "NA", "error"))

Arguments

x

A vector.

ties

Character string specifying how ties should be handled. One of:

"first"

Return the first mode encountered (default).

"all"

Return all modes.

"NA"

Return a missing value if multiple modes exist.

"error"

Throw an error if the mode is not unique.

Value

Depending on ties:

  • "first" returns a single value of the same type as x.

  • "all" returns a vector containing all modal values.

  • "NA" returns a missing value of the same type as x when ties occur.

  • "error" returns a single value if the mode is unique, otherwise throws an error.

If x contains only missing values, a missing value of the same type as x is returned.

Details

The function is named calc_mode() rather than mode() so that it does not mask base::mode(), which reports the storage type of an object.

Examples

calc_mode(c(1, 2, 2, 3))
#> [1] 2

calc_mode(c(1, 1, 2, 2), ties = "all")
#> [1] 1 2

calc_mode(c("a", "b", "a"))
#> [1] "a"

calc_mode(c(NA, 1, 1, 2))
#> [1] 1
